# Import Libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)
library(readxl)
```



# Data importation
```{r}
data=read_excel("dtcln.xlsx")
head(data)
```


# Data stracture
```{r}
str(data)
```


# Check for missing values
```{r}
colSums(is.na(data))
```


# Separate continuous and categorical variables
```{r}
continuous_vars <- c(
  "Age",
  "Income_KES",
  "Household_Size",
  "Farm_Size_Acres",
  "Monthly_Expenses_KES",
  "Years_Experience"
)

categorical_vars <- c(
  "Education",
  "Gender",
  "Extension_Access",
  "Adoption_Status"
)
head(continuous_vars)
```


# Check missing values in continuous variables
```{r}
colSums(is.na(data[continuous_vars]))
```


# Replace missing continuous values with the MEAN
```{r}
for (var in continuous_vars) {
  
  data[[var]][is.na(data[[var]])] <- 
    mean(data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
}
colSums(is.na(data[continuous_vars]))
```


# Replace missing continuous values with the MEDIAN
```{r}
for (var in continuous_vars) {
  
  data[[var]][is.na(data[[var]])] <- 
    median(data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
}
```


# Find the mode for categorical variables
# R does not have a simple built-in mode() function for statistical mode, so we create one:
```{r}
get_mode <- function(x) {
  
  ux <- unique(na.omit(x))
  
  ux[which.max(
    tabulate(match(x, ux))
  )]
}
get_mode(data$Gender)
```


# Replace missing categorical values with the MODE
```{r}
for (var in categorical_vars) {
  
  mode_value <- get_mode(data[[var]])
  
  data[[var]][is.na(data[[var]])] <- mode_value
}
colSums(is.na(data[categorical_vars]))
```


# investigate OUTLIERS
```{r}
summary(data[continuous_vars])
```

# Simple case
```{r}
boxplot(data$Income_KES)
```


# Boxplot of all continuous variables
```{r}
boxplot(
  data[continuous_vars],
  main = "Boxplots of Continuous Variables",
  las = 2,
  col = "lightblue"
)
```


# Scale the continuous variables
```{r}
scaled_data <- scale(data[continuous_vars])
scaled_data <- as.data.frame(scaled_data)
head(scaled_data)
```


# Boxplot of SCALED continuous variables
```{r}
boxplot(
  scaled_data,
  main = "Boxplots of Scaled Continuous Variables",
  las = 2,
  col = "lightgreen"
)
```


# Important; Scaling does NOT remove outliers. It only puts variables on a common scale. The outlier remains an outlier after scaling.


# Identify outliers using the IQR method
```{r}
find_outliers <- function(x) {
  
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  IQR_value <- Q3 - Q1
  
  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_value
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_value
  
  which(x < lower | x > upper)
}
```


# Test
```{r}
find_outliers(data$Income_KES)
find_outliers(data$Farm_Size_Acres)
```


# Count outliers in every continuous variable
```{r}
outlier_count <- sapply(
  data[continuous_vars],
  function(x) length(find_outliers(x))
)

outlier_count
```


# Replace outliers with the MEDIAN
# We use the median because it is resistant to extreme observations.
```{r}
replace_outliers_median <- function(x) {
  
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  IQR_value <- Q3 - Q1
  
  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_value
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_value
  
  median_value <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  x[x < lower | x > upper] <- median_value
  
  return(x)
}

for (var in continuous_vars) {
  
  data[[var]] <- replace_outliers_median(data[[var]])
}
```


# Check the boxplots again
```{r}
boxplot(
  data[continuous_vars],
  main = "Continuous Variables After Outlier Treatment",
  las = 2,
  col = "lightblue"
)
```


# Scaled data
```{r}
scaled_data <- as.data.frame(
  scale(data[continuous_vars])
)

boxplot(
  scaled_data,
  main = "Boxplots of Scaled Continuous Variables After Outlier Treatment",
  las = 2
)
```
